messages:
anya: Customer 'BrightForms' is seeing 403s intermittently since we rolled their service key. Reporting same error across two projects under the org. Req IDs: r-1a2b3c4d, r-1a2b3c5e. Can we collect reproduction steps and a debug bundle?

mike: Can you paste the failing curl (sanitized) and the exact response body + status? Need to check whether the call is hitting the right org/project headers.

anya: Here is the sanitized curl they sent:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: org-brightforms' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"test"}'
```
Response snippet they attached: `{"error":"forbidden","message":"org mismatch","request_id":"r-1a2b3c4d"}` HTTP/1.1 403

sam: Two quick triage bits: 1) is the service key scoped to a project or org? 2) are we seeing any proxy rewrite that changes org header?

irene: I checked the request logs for r-1a2b3c4d — on our edge it landed with `X-Forwarded-Org: org-brightforms` but downstream auth saw `org: org-brightforms-prod` (different). Looks like a header mutation in the internal gateway for some routes.

mike: Can you grab the full upstream/downstream headers for one of the request IDs and paste them here (sanitized)? Also include the parsed token KID and aud if possible.

anya: Uploaded logs: upstream headers for r-1a2b3c4d -> `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX`, `X-Redwood-Org: org-brightforms` ; downstream auth service saw `authorization` header identical but `x-org` header = `org-brightforms-prod`. Token parsed as: kid=kb_12345 aud=api.redwood.ai scope=project:bf-forms`.

sam: That explains 403 — service key is project-scoped (scope contains `project:bf-forms`) but downstream mapping rewrote org to a prod org that doesn't match the project mapping. Two reproduction angles: A) show that sending the same curl without X-Redwood-Org (rely on token-scoped org) succeeds/fails B) a direct call to the auth service with the token to confirm allowed projects.

anya: Customer tried removing the `X-Redwood-Org` header and got 200 for a single request (r-1a2b3c5e) then subsequent ones went 403 again. Very flaky.

infra-bot: debug-bundle-requested: id=db-20240715-9f12, include: edge logs, gateway headers, auth service trace, token parse dump. Use `#support` to track progress.

mike: Next steps: 1) Get the debug bundle from customer (we asked for db id). 2) Infra to trace gateway rule changes around the time of rotation (config commit id?). 3) Support to ask customer for a curl with `--trace-ascii` and one with the header removed.

irene: Found a recent rollback of a header-translation rule on gateway node pool A at 2024-07-15T03:14Z — that could cause intermittent mismatches across nodes. I'm pulling the request trace for r-1a2b3c4d and r-1a2b3c5e and will attach.

anya: I told the customer to collect `curl -v --trace-ascii out.txt ...` and to run 5 quick requests: 2 with `X-Redwood-Org`, 2 without, 1 with a fresh token. Also asked for the token KID/issued_at (sanitized).

sam: If we confirm gateway pool inconsistency, mitigation: pin the customer to routes served by pool B while we fix the rule, or enable our header-preservation fallback. I can prepare a short rollback playbook.

mike: Assigning to eng-oncall for escalation if infra trace shows config flip. @irene can you attach the traces here when ready?

irene: Attaching trace snippets (sanitized) and gateway commit id: commit-8f7a2. Evidence shows two different header mappings between nodes. I'll open a quick PR to stop the translation until we roll the fix.

anya: Thanks — customer guidance sent. I'll update the ticket with debug bundle id `db-20240715-9f12` and our internal trace links. Will circle back when PR merges. :thumbsup:
